column1: # DSP48E2 attribute table for Vivado fuzzing job 2
# One row per variant run. Columns (tab-separated):
# - id: stable run id, `v<nnn>`. The baseline is `v000` (all defaults).
# - attribute: DSP48E2 primitive attribute name, exactly as in the
#   BitFiltrator dsp.v template (the job-2 baseline design).
# - kind: string (Verilog string literal), int (bare integer), or
# - default: the dsp.v default value. Variant: the non-default value to
#   fuzz. Both are rendered verbatim into the variant Verilog by
#   gen_dsp_variants.py, except string values, which the generator
# Defaults and legal values are copied from the dsp.v comments in the
# tcl/dsp.v), which documents each attribute's legal values. No bit
# positions are claimed here: the whole point of job 2 is to measure
# Variant values are chosen as minimal non-default changes: one enum
# step, one register-stage step, one inversion bit, or a single-bit
# change to a 48-bit constant. A variant whose .rbt diff against the
# baseline is empty is a RESULT, not a failure: record it. (Example:
# XORSIMD only takes effect when USE_WIDEXOR is TRUE, so the XORSIMD
# variant alone may show no diff. Do not silently re-run it combined
# with USE_WIDEXOR=TRUE as the primary run; log a follow-up run
# instead, in runs.txt, with both attributes named.)
# Count: 46 attributes, 55 variants, 56 runs including the baseline.
# The instructions estimate 60-100 runs; 56 is the single-attribute
# sweep. Follow-up combined runs (see JOB2.md) are extra, and are
# logged separately, never folded into the primary table.
